account: On the night of Saturday 13 June 2026, Phú Thọ provincial police detected a group of teenagers gathering in Việt Trì ward. Officers were monitoring and mining data from the camera system. Tuổi Trẻ reports that police found the group through camera monitoring and tips from residents. It reported on 14 June that the teenagers were preparing weapons and vehicles to fight and disturb public order. Within about 30 minutes the AI camera system of the provincial command center had accurately identified the faces of all 18 participants. They were aged 14 to 18. They came from Việt Trì, Vân Phú and Nông Trang wards and Phù Ninh and Bình Phú communes (Tuổi Trẻ, VietNamNet). Tiền Phong says that the whole case was clarified in just over two hours. It says that 17 of the 18 were pupils of schools including Vũ Thê Lang High School and Dữu Lâu Middle School. One had dropped out. It says that the provincial police summoned all 18, and that at the police station they admitted the violations. None of the reports of 14 June says whether a fight took place. On 19 June 2026 Phú Thọ police said that two groups had fought with knives, swords, tridents and glass beer bottles at the Hội Thịnh roundabout around 23:30 on 13 June. They charged 10 people aged 16 to 18 with public disorder (Thanh Niên). One was detained, and nine were barred from leaving their place of residence. Thanh Niên describes most of the 10 as workers. The reports do not say whether these 10 are among the 18 identified by camera.

ai_role.statement: Police found the gathering through camera monitoring together with tips from residents. The facial recognition of the provincial AI camera network then supplied the identities of all 18 in about 30 minutes, per the police account. Officers verified the matches and summoned and questioned the 18. No source names a vendor or an algorithm or gives an accuracy figure, and every source relays the provincial police.

fields.account: On the night of Saturday 13 June 2026, Phú Thọ provincial police detected a group of teenagers gathering in Việt Trì ward. Officers were monitoring and mining data from the camera system. Tuổi Trẻ reports that police found the group through camera monitoring and tips from residents. It reported on 14 June that the teenagers were preparing weapons and vehicles to fight and disturb public order. Within about 30 minutes the AI camera system of the provincial command center had accurately identified the faces of all 18 participants. They were aged 14 to 18. They came from Việt Trì, Vân Phú and Nông Trang wards and Phù Ninh and Bình Phú communes (Tuổi Trẻ, VietNamNet). Tiền Phong says that the whole case was clarified in just over two hours. It says that 17 of the 18 were pupils of schools including Vũ Thê Lang High School and Dữu Lâu Middle School. One had dropped out. It says that the provincial police summoned all 18, and that at the police station they admitted the violations. None of the reports of 14 June says whether a fight took place. On 19 June 2026 Phú Thọ police said that two groups had fought with knives, swords, tridents and glass beer bottles at the Hội Thịnh roundabout around 23:30 on 13 June. They charged 10 people aged 16 to 18 with public disorder (Thanh Niên). One was detained, and nine were barred from leaving their place of residence. Thanh Niên describes most of the 10 as workers. The reports do not say whether these 10 are among the 18 identified by camera.
fields.summary: On 13 June 2026 Phú Thọ police saw teenagers preparing weapons to fight in Việt Trì, and the provincial AI camera system identified all 18 faces in about 30 minutes.
